Kuvitus: pyöräilijä ajaa hämärässä metsä: Illustration: a cyclist rides along a forest road at dusk. The dynamo is in the hub of the front wheel of the bicycle, and the lamp on the handlebars shines: the beam of light falls on the road in front of the wheel. The sky is evening blue, and spruces stand at the edge of the road.
Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa: Faradayn: Schematic picture, not to scale: Faraday's experiment in three stages. In each picture a wire coil is connected to a voltmeter. On the left a bar magnet is pushed north pole first towards the coil and into it, and the needle of the meter deflects to the right. In the middle the magnet is at rest inside the coil, and the needle is at zero. On the right the magnet is pulled out of the coil, and the needle deflects to the left.
Periaatekuva sivulta, kolme osaa: vaakas: Schematic picture from the side, three parts: horizontal green field lines point from left to right, and a wire loop is seen edge-on as a narrow oval. On the left the plane of the loop is perpendicular to the field, and five field lines pass through the loop: the flux is B times A. In the middle the loop is tilted, and only three lines pass through it: the flux is smaller. On the right the plane of the loop is parallel to the field, and no line passes through it: the flux is zero.
Kaksi kuvaajaa mittakaavassa samalla aik: Two graphs to scale on the same time axis from zero to four seconds. A square coil of ten turns, side 0.10 m, moves at a speed of 0.10 m/s through a region of magnetic field of 0.20 T. Upper graph: the magnetic flux in milliwebers is zero until 0.5 seconds, grows steadily to 2.0 at 1.5 s, stays constant until 2.5 seconds and decreases steadily to zero at 3.5 s. Lower graph: the induced voltage in millivolts is zero when the flux does not change, minus 20 while the flux grows and plus 20 while the flux decreases. Dashed lines at 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 and 3.5 s link the graphs. In the top right corner of the figure is the label N = 10 turns.
Periaatekuva ylhäältä, ei mittakaavassa:: Schematic picture from above, not to scale: two horizontal metal rails whose left ends are joined to a voltmeter. On the rails is a vertical copper rod that moves to the right at velocity v. The magnetic field points into the paper, shown by evenly spaced green crosses. In the middle of the rod is an electron, on which the magnetic force points downwards and the electric force upwards. Electrons have collected at the lower end of the rod, which is negative, and the upper end is positive. In the rod the electric field points from top to bottom. The distance between the rails, that is, the length of the rod in the field, is l.
Illustration: a shake-powered torch on a table. Inside the transparent body is a cylindrical magnet, and in the middle of the body is a copper coil. When the torch is shaken, the magnet slides back and forth through the coil, and the LED at the front of the torch shines.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: käämin läpi kulke: Graph to scale: the magnetic flux through the coil in milliwebers as a function of time in seconds. The flux grows steadily from zero to 4.0 between 0 and 0.20 s, stays at 4.0 until 0.50 s, decreases steadily to zero by 0.60 s and is zero after that. The grid spacing is 0.1 s and 1 mWb.
